section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: The natural order in which the four language skills are normally acquired is:
explanation: LSRW — Listening and Speaking (receptive-then-productive oral skills) precede Reading and Writing (literacy skills), mirroring first-language acquisition.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: An English teacher conducts the whole class only in English, uses real objects and gestures, and never translates into the mother tongue. This is characteristic of the:
explanation: The Direct Method teaches the target language through the target language, using demonstration and context instead of translation. Grammar-Translation relies heavily on the mother tongue and rule learning.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: Which pair correctly classifies the language skills as receptive?
explanation: Receptive (input) skills are listening and reading; productive (output) skills are speaking and writing.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: Quickly running the eyes over a timetable to find the departure time of one train is an example of:
explanation: Scanning searches a text for a specific piece of information. Skimming reads rapidly to get the general idea/gist; intensive reading is close study of a short text.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: A test that asks pupils to write an original paragraph describing their village is best described as a:

options.option_text: Subjective / essay-type item assessing productive writing
Objective item with a single correct answer
A test of listening comprehension only

explanation: Free composition has many acceptable answers and needs judgement to score — a subjective/essay-type item testing productive writing. Objective items (MCQ, matching) have a single fixed key.
